newsitem.title: USA: Florida has sold some 80 pct of tobacco holdings.
newsitem.headline: Florida has sold some 80 pct of tobacco holdings.

text.p: Florida sold nearly $650 million in cigarette company stocks in a little over three weeks last month after the state decided to dump tobacco from its pension plan portfolio, state officials said Monday.

Officials in Florida, one of many states waging legal battles against big tobacco, voted on May 28 to jettison the highly profitable cigarette component of the state's $69 billion employee pension fund.

By Monday, nearly 78 percent of the tobacco portfolio had been quietly sold, said Tom Herndon, executive director of the Florida Department of Administration. About $185 million in tobacco company stock remained in the fund.

Florida sold about 16 million shares of stock, including 10.6 million shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc between May 30 and June 20, when a proposed national settlement was announced between tobacco companies and 40 states, including Florida, that are suing to recoup the public health costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.
Noting that the stocks' prices dropped after the settlement, Herndon said the portfolio's managers decided to stop divesting.

"The stocks dropped about $4 or $5 a share over the next several days for Philip Morris. With Congressional hearings starting, we just said under the circumstances, let's hold out for a little while here," he said.

Florida's Medicaid suit against tobacco is scheduled to go to trial on August 4 in West Palm Beach, and state officials have insisted they will press the suit in spite of Florida's involvement in negotiations for the industrywide settlement.

"The stocks have been very volatile and that volatility increases the risk," said Ryan Banfill, spokesman for Fla. Gov. Lawton Chiles. "The governor is pleased that the state is purging these stocks."
